stories.author: Judd Legum
stories.title: PopInfo Weekly: Fantasies, fabrications, and fuel
stories.text: Elon Musk, the world’s richest person, is funding an aggressive advertising campaign encouraging people in key states to check their registration status on votesafe.org. Musk’s website collects extensive personal information from users, profiles them and tracks their internet use. It then shares this data with X, Meta, Google, and other online advertising companies. This week, in the lead-up to the 25th anniversary of 9/11, President Trump pushed a false personal narrative of the attack. Most notably, he claimed to have sent 100 of his own construction workers to Ground Zero to help clear rubble. However, the Trump Organization had only around a dozen employees at the time, and Trump’s construction projects were being run by contractors. American workers are taking home a historically low share of the value they produce, according to data released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). In the second quarter of 2026, the labor share of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) hit its lowest level since the BLS first began tracking it in 1947. stories.author: Ken Klippenstein
stories.title: Fuck 9/11
stories.text: Union Square memorial to those killed on 9/11, on September 18, 2001 | Getty Twenty-five years later, 9/11 anniversaries have devolved into a grotesque fundraising orgy for the security state. The families commemorate their loved ones while the very security institutions that failed to prevent the attack in the first place tell triumphant war stories and warn that if we (the American people) let down our guard — by which they mean close our wallets to them — it will happen again. “The 9/11 attack took place without warning,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio writes to his employees today, per a memo leaked to me. After opening with chest-beating (“We have hunted down the architects of the attack…”), practically all he can say is: don’t let your guard down . Rubio memo 1.7MB ∙ PDF file Download Download When it comes to the 9/11 anniversary, fundraising has become more and more dominant. But it used to have a heart as well. stories.title: How Ansarallah Swept Past Saudi-Backed Forces to Control Yemen’s Red Sea Coast
stories.text: Yemen’s Ansarallah completed their control of the Bab al-Mandab on Friday following sweeping gains yesterday in the most significant shift in territorial control in five years of the country’s long-running civil war. Following days of escalating fighting in the western mountains of Taiz governorate, Saudi-backed forces of the Internationally Recognized Government (IRG) of Yemen appeared to collapse on Thursday, allowing Ansarallah, also known as the Houthis, to seize the strategically important port-city of Mocha. On Friday, Ansarallah forces took Mayum island, also known as Perim, which lies on the Yemeni side of the Bab al-Mandab Strait two miles off Yemen’s west coast. The small volcanic island acts as a natural choke point in the strait, narrowing the Red Sea channel to nine miles from the coast of Djibouti. Ansarallah fighters posted videos online of military vehicles driving down the runway—built in 2022 by the United Arab Emirates—at Mocha’s newly developed airport. Footage also showed detainees being released from the city’s central prison as Ansarallah took control. The advance puts the Houthis in direct control of one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes. stories.title: Democrats Are Urging Trump to Re-Escalate on North Korea
stories.text: Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., walks down the House steps after the last votes of the week in the U.S. This article is being co-published with Capital & Empire . Earlier this month, a coalition of 50 antiwar and foreign policy groups reached out to the top Democrats on the House Foreign Affairs Committee with an unusual plea: Please don’t attack President Trump—at least not for his decision to de-escalate tensions with North Korea as he focuses his attention on the Mideast. The groups were worried that an almost instinctual Democratic response to Trump’s decision to scale back military exercises with South Korea would be to attack him from a hawkish direction, call him weak on national security, and demand ever more confrontation. Instead, they suggested, take the win, and celebrate the reduction in hostile tension. The advice was not taken.
